Life chances for all
Welcome to Knowl Hill School
Welcome to Knowl Hill School, an independent, co-educational school nestled in the picturesque villages of Pirbright and Bisley in Surrey. We specialise in supporting students with a range of complex and co-occuring needs. Many of our students have specific learning difficulties such as dyslexia, dyspraxia, and dyscalculia, along with diagnoses such as ADHD, sensory sensitivities, development language disorders (DLD), hypermobility, autism and anxiety. All our pupils have transitioned from mainstream educational settings, where they had often experienced repeated academic struggles, bullying, and social isolation. We understand that sensory overload is a significant challenge for many of them. At Knowl Hill, we provide a safe and nurturing environment where every student feels supported and accepted. Our goal is to empower our students to rediscover their confidence, unlock their potential and thrive both in learning and in life.

pageCache.pageTitle: Knowl Hill School - Careers and Work Experience
pageCache.text:
Careers and Work Experience
Work experience is a valuable part of our school's approach to preparing students for life beyond the classroom. It provides students with an opportunity to step into the world of work, gaining first-hand insight into different industries, careers, and workplace expectations. By spending time in a professional environment, students develop essential skills such as communication, teamwork, time management, and problem-solving. This practical exposure helps bridge the gap between academic learning and real-world application, allowing students to better understand how their studies relate to future career paths.
Beyond skill development, work experience encourages self-confidence and independence. It helps students discover their strengths and interests, which can be incredibly useful when making future choices about further education or employment. Many students return from their placements with a clearer sense of direction and a renewed motivation to achieve their goals. At our school, we believe that offering structured, meaningful work experience is a crucial step in equipping students for success in an ever-changing world.

Pupil Absences
Please see below the request for pupil absences form.
If you wish to request time away from Knowl Hill School, you will need to complete a pupil absence request form. This will need to be addressed to Dr Govender, and he will review each request and respond with an outcome. Absence will only be approved for exceptional circumstances. (Family bereavement, Emergency medical/hospital appointments and Religious Observances are usually seen as exceptional circumstances.)
Request for Pupil Absence

Prospectus
Whether you're a prospective parent, pupil, or simply interested in learning more about what makes our school unique, our prospectus is a great place to start. You’ll find information about our ethos, the day-to-day life of the school, our approach to learning, and the supportive community that underpins everything we do.
We hope it gives you a real sense of what it means to be part of Knowl Hill. If you have any further questions or would like to arrange a visit, please don’t hesitate to get in touch — we’d be very happy to welcome you.

pageCache.pageTitle: Knowl Hill School - Residential Trips and Outdoor Learning
pageCache.text:
Residential Trips and Outdoor Learning
A key part of Knowl Hill Schools curriculum is outdoor learning which we introduce through activities such as Forest School. Outdoor learning is included in both the lower and the senior school, enabling all students to become immersed in nature. As well as learning through Forest School, students get the opportunity to participate in residential trips including a residential experience at the Tile barn (Lower school), and a 3-day Bushcraft residential in North Yorkshire. The residential trips help students engage in new activities as well as developing their personal skills and making memories.
Forest School is a timetabled curriculum subject, up to and including year 9. After year 9, students are given the choice as to whether they’d like to continue.
Forest School activities take place in a dedicated area at the Surrey Wildlife Trust and its surrounding woodland.
Within the Forest School program, students are able to develop an intuitive attitude to tasks such as risk assessments, which allow them to safely operate in the forest. They will learn to work with a variety of tools as well as managing campfires. Other activities that they will participate in include:
Rope work
Making shelters
Creating objects such as swings and chairs
Teamwork exercises

Safeguarding
At Know Hill School, safeguarding is our highest priority. We want to ensure that all children are safe, happy and secure at all times.
Knowl Hill Safeguarding Policy Statement
The welfare of the child is paramount, and safeguarding all members of our school community underpins everything that we do. We recognise that children have a right to feel safe and secure, they cannot learn effectively unless they do so. All children have a right to be protected from harm and abuse.
We recognise that all staff have a role in the prevention of harm and abuse and an equal responsibility to act immediately on any suspicion or disclosure that may indicate a child is at risk of harm. With this in mind, all members of staff receive regular training in identifying and raising child protection concerns, dealing appropriately with disclosures, and handling sensitively issues around online safety, sexual health and appropriate relationships, and drugs and alcohol awareness.
Prevent Duty is part of the UK government’s counter-terrorism strategy, CONTEST. Its aim is to stop people becoming terrorists or supporting terrorism.
From 1st July, the Counter Terrorism and Security Act 2015 places a statutory duty on specified authorities to have “due regard to the need to prevent people from being drawn into terrorism”. The strategy involves thousands of people – police and intelligence officers, the emergency services, local authorities, businesses, voluntary and community organisations, governments and other partners – working together across the UK and the world to protect the public.
Parents and carers play a role in safeguarding children in their community. If you have any concerns about your own child, or another, please do not hesitate to contact one of our Safeguarding Leads or send an email to the school’s safeguarding team: safeguarding@khs.education.

To report an emergency concern please refer to Surrey County Council's Children's Services contact page, which includes an out of hours number. If you think a child or young person may be in immediate danger call 999.
Helpful Links: NSPCC - PANTS Guides NSPCC - Keeping Children Safe
NSPCC - 0808 800 5000
Child Line - 0800 1111 CEOP Education (protecting children online*).
If you have a problem or concern in school or at home you can report it to a member of staff or use the following email: safeguarding@khs.education
We want everyone in our school to feel safe, supported, and heard. That’s why we also use Whisper – an anonymous reporting tool that lets students share concerns quickly, securely, and anonymously if needed.
Whisper is a safe and anonymous way for you to report anything that’s worrying you – whether it affects you directly or someone else. It connects directly with our safeguarding team, who will review and respond to every message received
You can send a message using the Whisper link below or text your concern directly to our confidential Whisper number.
You do not need to give your name unless you choose to. All messages are seen only by our safeguarding team. All concerns are taken seriously and treated with respect.
https://swgfl.org.uk/whisper/khs2/
Is It Really Anonymous?
Yes — if you want it to be. Whisper allows you to report something without giving your name, unless you choose to include it. Your message will go straight to the school’s safeguarding tea,, who will take appropriate action
Even if you stay anonymous, we will still investigate and follow up the concern.
If you don’t want to use Whisper, that’s okay. You can also speak to a trusted adult in school.
Speaking up is never wrong. Whether you use Whisper or another way to reach out, we’re here to help.
Visitors to Our School
Please familiarise yourself with the guidance in our visitor’s leaflet to prepare for your visit.

By doing this, we allow students to develop an understanding of the core principles of sciences such as, energy, forces, cell biology, and particle physics. Students are then able to develop their knowledge as they move up in the school whilst still being hands on by partaking in experiments and activities.

pageCache.pageTitle: Knowl Hill School - Readers and Scribes
pageCache.text:
Readers and Scribes
Readers/Scribes must abide by the regulations since failure to do so could lead to the disqualification of the candidate.
They are not able to guide a candidate through their exam paper. It is the child’s responsibility to direct the exam and to instruct the facilitator.
Readers can read the instructions on the question paper and the questions to the candidate but must not explain or clarify. This may involve reading the whole paper or the candidate may request only some words to be read.
For GCSE English Language or Functional Skills and Entry Level English Reading Papers – Candidates entitled to a Reader, a human reader is not permitted (in section A for GCSE or the entire paper for Functional Skills/Entry Level). However, candidates can opt to use a Computer Reader or a Reading Pen – for which they have been assessed – and can practise in English lessons.
Scribes write down or word processes the candidate’s dictated answers. Candidates are expected to dictate punctuation and grammar, identifying when headings and new paragraphs are required. Scribes may not add punctuation/grammar unless it is dictated by the candidate.
Candidates using a Scribe can access marks for Spelling, Punctuation & Grammar (SPAG) dependent on if they dictate their spelling, punctuation and grammar. A JCQ Scribe Cover Sheet is attached to scripts indicating what was dictated during the exam.

Knowl Hill School - Where Learning and Life Skills Flourish
At Knowl Hill School, we believe that every child deserves a chance to reach their full potential, regardless of learning needs. We are a specialist school dedicated to supporting students aged 10-16 who have dyslexia or other co-occurring needs such as Developmental Language Disorder (DLD) and Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD).
We are more than just an educational institution; Knowl Hill is a nurturing environment where students find the support and resources they need to thrive academically, personally, and emotionally. Departments
At Knowl Hill School, we pride ourselves in having a varied and detailed curriculum that helps to benefit our students. Our curriculum is tailored for students with dyslexia and other co-occurring needs, so they aren't at a disadvantage and that students have the ability to thrive.
As a school, we value the opportunity that we have to help nurture and support students in their understanding of subjects as well as helping them to enjoy and love learning. Having a diverse curriculum allows students to gain exposure in all aspects of learning with the support of caring and knowledgeable staff.
To find out more about individual subject/department, please choose one from the list on the right hand side of the page.

Maths
Maths is one of the three core subjects, meaning that it is a compulsory subject. Whilst maths can be intimidating to learn, at Knowl Hill School, we help to guide students through the subject, one step at a time, helping to build their understanding as well as their confidence.
Maths is a skill that is essential to everyday life. Therefore, a high-quality maths education is crucial for students as it helps to develop an understanding of the world, the ability to reason mathematically as well as making maths enjoyable.
Multi-sensory strategies used in maths include:
The courses we offer are made as visual and kinaesthetic as possible as well as using software and website that are dyslexia friendly. Even if students don’t want a career in maths, confidence with numbers is a great skill to have for everyday life.
AQA Mathematics - 8300
A maths GCSE shows that students have an understanding of numbers as well as the ability to work with them. In the AQA GCSE maths course students will build on the basics which they will have covered lower down in the school including learning to solve numerical problems and make calculations. They’ll learn about number systems and shapes and progress to algebraic equations, formulae, graphs and functions. Students will also learn to collect and assess mathematical data and use it to solve specific problems.
AQA GCSE Statistics - 8382
Students studying for GCSE Mathematics will be given the opportunity to broaden their knowledge in a key component of maths that is relevant in everyday life. They’ll develop a core statistical grounding, as well as transferable skills and understanding that’s applicable to a range of other subjects. It’ll also benefit students who wish to progress onto A-level subjects such as science, geography and psychology,
There is an expectation that students completing GCSE maths and statistics are required to complete regular homework tasks.
TQU Functional Skills Mathematics (Level 1/Level 2) and AQA Entry Level Certificate (5930)
For the students who find maths more challenging, we offer both TQU Functional Skills Mathematics at Level 1 and 2 as well as AQA Entry Level Certificate Mathematics at Level 1, 2 and 3, which are taken in stages over 2 years. These courses concentrate on the maths needed in everyday life such as reading a timetable and using money.

Our Governors
Let us introduce you to our Board of Governors!
James Cooke - Director (Chairperson)
Email - Jcooke@khs.education
About James - "I was born and raised in a seaside village in New Zealand, where I played and coached rugby, served as a lifeguard for the Surf Living Saving Club and as a crew member of the RNLI lifeboat that was stationed in my village.
I taught for 7 years and served as a Headteacher in a village school for 4 years. I then moved to the UK and taught in both primary and secondary schools before taking up the position of Headteacher in a village primary school in Berkshire. I retired after 29 years in this job. I continue to work with aspiring leaders as a coach and through the National Professional Qualification (NPQ) program.
I am married with 4 children, with one of my sons having Dyslexia which meant like many parents, we had to fight to have his needs recognised and for the appropriate provisions to meet his need. I was invited to join the board in 2021."
About Russ - "I started teaching after graduating from Leeds University, having subsequently completed a post graduate Certificate in Education. I later gained an MA in Education focusing on Curriculum Studies, and continued as a teacher then head teacher, acquiring the National Professional Qualification for Headship. My career included work in Yorkshire, Iran and Saudi Arabia, after which as an assessor and coach, I worked for the National College for School Leadership. I have experience of school governance in Woking, including several Ofsted Inspections.
My wife and one of my daughters are teachers. I believe strongly in equality of opportunity for all children to achieve, and was impressed - following a recent visit - by the provision at Knowl Hill. I hope to support the schools ongoing mission to provide the very best environment for children to achieve and for staff, students and, parents to work together with purpose and rigour.
Now that the school year is underway, I plan to find time to come along and observe some classes. Although I have already gained useful insights into what makes the diverse and energetic pupils tick, I want to get to know the staff better. I plan to focus on how the teachers provide learning opportunities that challenge and encourage learners, how they gain the interest of students, and how they motivate them to work hard and take risks, not fearing errors but using them for their learning. Given the small class sizes, and despite the diversity of needs, I hope to see teachers and students gaining satisfaction from their work. An area of significant interest will be how staff with leadership responsibilities manage to support and develop their colleagues.
Anna Rhodes - Director (Therapy)
About Anna - "I was invited to join the board in 2016, after I'd enjoyed 6 and a half years of working with students and staff at Knowl Hill as the first Speech and Language Therapist to be employed directly by the school.
During my time working at the school, I built up a sound knowledge base of the difficulties encountered by young people who struggled with language and literacy and, on the strength of this, I published a book of resources for teenagers with language difficulties, which is still selling well to this day. I completed my Masters in Special Education whilst working at Knowl Hill.
I am married with 2 sons, both of whom have high level difficulties with literacy and so my experience with dyslexia is both professional and personal.
I have continued to work as a Speech and Language Therapist, where I'm currently working part-time in the assessment centre in a special school. I also practice as a Registered Intermediary to support the communication between vulnerable witnesses and the judiciary system."
Maureen Spencer - Director (Safeguarding)
About Maureen - "I am recently retired from North Surrey Magistrates, having sat in both the adult and family courts for 26 years. In my early career, I qualified as a general nurse and Health Visitor before having my family. I have 3 grown up sons and many grandchildren, so I regularly help with childcare."
Nora Leggett - Director (Finance)
About Nora - "I am delighted to join the board. After graduating with a combined Arts Degree (English, French and German), I joined Hertz UK's graduate training scheme and settled into a general management career lasting over 40 years in the automotive sector. As a chartered member of the Institute of Personnel & Development (CIPD), I have held various operational roles in my career with HR and learning and development specialisms at their core. Supporting young people so that they benefit from the tailored education offered at Knowl Hill School is my ambition but also that they see enacted in practice the solid principles of fairness, opportunity, tolerance and respect for difference - important social values that are increasingly important in the world of work. I have built a sound network throughout my professional life and I look forwards to serving on the Board and adding value wherever I can. Reading with students on an individual and group basis is one of the highlights of my week and I thoroughly enjoy my Friday morning visits to the school. Professionally, I have considerable experience in running a not-for-profit organisation and, recently retired, I now take an active role in business accounting for the Knowl Hill Foundation, and particularly the development of the new school campus at Bisley. I am an active member of the KHS Finance Committee where I have responsibility for researching grants from potential funders to help us with our expenditure on buildings and equipment. To kit-out a single modern classroom with all the latest technology can cost anything up to £20,000 - so it is important that we try and secure funding and donations (monetary and equipment) from as many sources as we can. So, if there is any parent or carer who would like to make a donation or who has contacts in IT and technology companies (e.g., servers, laptops, whiteboards, CCTV and other security applications) - I'd be delighted to hear from you. You can contact me via the school office."
